properties.name: REFUTED — flo2's per-call retention hypothesis, tested by its own named falsification: 140 export-free calls reach 101 MB and a 128-call mixed workload 173 MB, against a predicted 186-526
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-09-13, same box and same rig as the root-cause finding, two fresh servers on identical copies of reflow2's own 4,403-node store. ZERO exports in either arm.

THE HYPOTHESIS, from flo2 the same day: retention tracks CALL COUNT rather than payload size, because their 448 MB server had served 140 calls of which only nine were exports (~3.8 MB of document in total). Applying per-call rates read off the reflow2 ladder to flo2's 131 non-export calls predicted 186-526 MB. flo2 flagged it as hypothesis, not measurement, and named its own falsification: run ~140 export-free calls; per-call retention says it approaches ~450 MB, and if it stays near 100 MB the hypothesis is dead.

THAT TEST WAS RUN, AS SPECIFIED.

  ARM H — 140 x graph_report, no exports:
      start 62 · 1 call 89 · 5 calls 100 · 10 calls 100 · 20 calls 101
      · 40 101 · 60 101 · 80 101 · 100 101 · 120 101 · 140 MB 101
    FLAT FROM CALL FIVE. Not 450. The hypothesis's own stated kill condition.

  ARM M — flo2's tool MIX, 128 non-export calls, no exports. Built to their
  distribution (loop_status, get_node, add_decision, create_edge, get_skill,
  scan_nodes, detect_gaps, search_design, what_next, graph_report, maturity_report,
  reviewed_gaps, describe_schema, claim_report, open_questions, sync_status,
  detect_defects), because 140 IDENTICAL calls warm one allocation path while a
  diverse mix could warm many — the one way the hypothesis could still have held:
      start 65 · 1 call 91 · 10 calls 100 · 25 137 · 50 138 · 75 167
      · 100 144 · 128 MB 173
    173 MB, below flo2's own lower bound of 186, and NON-MONOTONIC (167 -> 144 -> 173).

⭐ WHAT IS TRUE IN THE HYPOTHESIS, and it is the part worth keeping: ordinary calls DO accrue. Arm M moved 65 -> 173 MB, about 108 MB over 128 calls, and diversity accrues more than repetition (173 against 101). The mechanism flo2 describes is real. What is refuted is its MAGNITUDE and its SHAPE: the accrual is steeply front-loaded and saturates, so a flat per-call rate extrapolated over 131 calls is the wrong arithmetic. The reflow2 ladder already said so within its own ten points and neither side read it that way: call 1 of the ten graph_reports was +26 MB on its own and calls 6-10 moved it by 1 MB in total, so the "3.9 MB/call" input to the prediction was an average over a curve that had already flattened.

🛑 SO FLO2'S 448 MB IS STILL UNEXPLAINED, and it is now MORE anomalous rather than less. Their design is 202 nodes and 2.9 MB against this one's 4,403 and 14.7 MB, so every reply on their rig is SMALLER and the per-call accrual should be LOWER than what was measured here. 131 ordinary calls reached 173 MB on the larger design; the same count on the smaller one should reach less, not 448.

⭐ THE CANDIDATE THIS LEAVES, untested and cheap for flo2 to check: GLIBC'S ARENA COUNT SCALES WITH CORE COUNT. The default cap is 8 x the number of cores, and arena count is already confirmed here as the retaining mechanism — MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2 took the same five-export workload from 433 MB to 233 MB. This box has 4 cores (32-arena cap) and the live server runs 17 threads. A host with substantially more cores would retain proportionally more for the SAME workload, which is exactly the shape needed: two rigs reaching ~450 MB by different routes, one through five huge calls on a small-arena box and one through 140 ordinary calls on a large-arena one. FALSIFICATION FOR FLO2: report `nproc` on the host that produced 448 MB, then re-run the same session with MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2. If cores are high and the env var moves the number substantially, this holds; if cores are 4 or fewer, it is dead too.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: flo2's host core count, libc, and whether their server ran in a container with a different allocator. No arm here varied core count. The arena-count candidate is reasoned from a confirmed mechanism, not measured across hosts, and must not be treated as settled — the same error both sides have now made once each today.
